text: Good afternoon. I'm calling this meeting of the Finance and Operations Committee to order. My name is Dina Griffiths, and I'm joined by my colleagues, Mr. Carty and Mr. Pepper. Is there public comment? Okay, so no public comment today. We'll move on to the minutes. May I have a motion to approve the minutes of August 4th for the Finance and Operations Committee meeting? So moved. Second.

Thank you. It has been moved and seconded to approve the minutes of the August 4th Finance and Operations Committee meeting. All those in favor, say aye. Aye. Aye. We will now move on to the consent agenda. May I have a motion to approve the consent agenda? Madam Chair, I move to approve the consent agenda for the September 1st, 2026 Finance and Operations Committee meeting. Second. All those in favor? Thank you both. And all those in favor, say aye. Aye.

Aye. I don't believe there are any action items for today, so we'll move on to information items, and we will now start with 5.01, Business and Financial Services Renewal of IFB number 126-100, Wind and String Instrument Repair Services. This item will be presented by Ms. Andrea Filla, Director of Procurement and Risk Management. Thank you, Ms. Filla. Good evening, and thank you for having a meeting this evening so I could get all

these items started on your agenda. The first one, as mentioned, is the Wind and String Instrument Repair contract. This contract we actually have had in place. The current contract we have expires November 30th, 2026. This is the first renewal for this contract. We have an agreement with Brenda's Shop and Dave Violins to do these repairs for

the instruments, and we bring it before you this evening to be considered to move to either action or consent item on your September 15th meeting with school board on September 22nd. The amount of this contract is approximately $260,000. The vendors did maintain their current pricing for the repair services. Thank you, Ms. Filla. I just wanted to point out on board docs, I'm not able to

pull it up. I noticed that earlier today. The documents are there, and some you can pull up, and some you can't. I do have the information. I've seen it. But I just wanted to give you a heads-up on that. Did we have any questions on the-- Are you guys were not able to pull it up as well? Is that why? Oh, you do have it? Okay. Do you have any questions on the contract? Chair Griffiths, I did want to share that there's only one item that

has backup. All the other backup items are in the executive-only section of board docs. Oh, okay. That would explain that. Okay. All right. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. And thank you, Ms. Filla. I'm assuming this is a pretty straightforward contract, this is just a renewal. These are for instruments that LCPS owns that students borrow or rent from us, is that correct? That is correct. Mr. Pearson is here in the room. Okay, he's nodding.

So yes, that is correct, that these are for the school-owned violins, cellos, bass, the wind and string instruments that we, LCPS, purchase. And is there regular maintenance that occurs at the end of each year, or is it when an item breaks? Yes. Both. Mr. Pearson actually does an end-of-year process where we will get invoices for his end-of-year repairs as well as ongoing repairs if something should break or need maintenance during the school year.

And okay, I don't think I have any more questions. I think this is a pretty straightforward one. Thank you both. This is a straightforward contract. And again, Mr. Pearson, thank you so much. It means a lot to me, and the students, that there are extra instruments at the schools if they show an interest to try another instrument or try a instrument,

that they have that opportunity for a lower cost. So, I appreciate that. And with that, no other questions, right? So, no discussion. Based on the discussions, is the committee comfortable in putting this on consent? I am. All right. We'll go ahead and do that. Thank you. Now we move on to 5.02, a Business and Financial Services award,

IFB number 127-100, custodial supplies and equipment for ongoing needs. This will be presented by Ms. Filla, Director of Procurement and Risk Management. Thank you. This is a contract that we bring to you annually. Every year, we issue a new solicitation for the purchase of our custodial supplies. Two of the biggest items on here would be your toilet tissue and your paper towel. So, very important things, which also you will see the estimated value of this

award is $1.4 million. These items are all delivered centrally and then provided out to our schools as needed to replenish the inventory at our schools so the custodians are able to do their jobs within our schools. We bring this item before you this evening as our current contract is set to expire October 31, 2026, and we bring it before you to be presented at your September 15th item, our meeting as an action item or a consent item, and then move to the school

board consent agenda on September 22nd, 2026. The attachment you will see there are several vendors awarded these items. This was an IFB, so it was the lowest price on the specified item or acceptable substitute. Thank you, Ms. Filla. Any questions? Yes, Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. And once we approve this, are these prices locked in for the '26, '27 school year? These prices are locked in for the school year, unless something very strange

happens with paper. But we don't generally allow them to increase our IFBs because this is a one-year contract. And if a vendor were to come back and do that, we would go to the next low bid on the specified item. So these are prices for a period of one year. Okay. I'm just asking because of the expected increase in the cost of paper goods due to the tariffs on Canada. It was the only reason I was asking that. Yes, we are seeing some of that coming through as we speak. Okay. Thank you.

That's interesting. How much paper do we get from Canada? I'm curious. I do not know where our paper comes from, but generally, when there's a paper increase, it's a paper increase. Thank you. I was just thrown by that. Okay. So if there's no more discussion, if we could go ahead and put this on consent, how does everybody feel? I'm okay with that. All right. Great. We'll move that to consent, and thank you very much.

We're moving on to 5.03. Business and Financial Services Renewal, RFP number 232-268, tree services. This item is also being presented by Ms. Filla, Director of Procurement and Risk Management. Thank you. Thank you. This contract is being brought before you as the estimated value is $580,000. This is a contract for our facility operations team, and this contract is for tree services. The vendor is Brightview Landscape, so Blue Bell, Pennsylvania,

with the next contract starting December 1, 2026. This is the third renewal option on this contract and being brought before you this evening to either be moved to action or consent at your September 15th meeting and school board consent on September 22nd. Thank you, Ms. Filla. Any questions there? No. Oh, you do. I'm sorry. Ms. Ricard. Thank you, Madam Chair. Is there a per project limit on this contract?

No, this contract would not have a per project limit as it's not construction related. So this contract is for down tree removal, tree trimming, dead trees, those types of things. So there would not be a per project limit on this contract. Okay. And this is the fourth year? This is the third renewal option. We would have one more renewal with an optional fifth-year renewal.

And just out of curiosity, what's the largest size project that we have in a year under this contract? Do you know? Mr. Wilhead is coming up to address your question. Good evening. Hi. In general, these are ad hoc. So last year, we had some large ones to remove the invasive trees, the Tree of Heavens. It was, I think, in the $80,000 to $90,000 range. Generally, it's between $5,000 and $30,000 to remove what we call

declining or dead trees on the campuses that are safety risks, or when we move around the campuses to trim low-hanging bushes, trees, and things of that nature. If there was a larger endeavor, like if, say, we had to go in, we would investigate, "Hey, what we could break this into smaller sections so we're not," for lack of a better term, "affecting too much of a campus at one time." But for

the most part, they're smaller efforts centered around safety or, I guess, beautification of the areas. Does this also include invasive... I had a constituent ask me that lives next door to one of our schools. We share a property line with one of the neighbors that had some invasive poison ivy, actually, on her fence that was coming from the school site. So is it to remove those kind of things and- It can be. Okay.

Generally, we reserve this for trees or worse- Okay ... I guess. From a risk perspective, we want a professional. If it's a large diameter tree or if it's leaning on something where we need a crane or specialized piece of equipment. If it's smaller things like that, our in-house teams take care of those. Okay, great. Thank you so much. I also had a question on that. Oops, sorry. I thought you were going to mention invasive species destroying the trees as well,

so some trees have to be removed. Are you seeing that more happening? We work with some of the partners in the area. The Tree of Heaven is a host for the lanternflies. We've taken out hundreds of those over the last several years. In certain instances, the Bradford pear or the callery pear, we'll take those out to try to limit the spread of those. But for the most part, the techniques for that are done in conjunction with-- We're not aggressively

trying to remove invasive species. We're just trying the host of those species. If that helps. If that answers your question. It does. It's just something everybody's aware of right now. Yes. So I thought I'd ask. Thank you so much. How does everybody feel about going to consent? Okay, this will go to consent as well. Thank you very much. We will move to now item 5.04, Business and Financial Services

Renewal of RFP 252274, Playground Equipment and Related Product Services. Again, presented by Ms. Andrea Fillow, Director of Procurement and Risk Management. Thank you. Thank you. This contract has an estimated value of $4.4 million. This is related to the projects that were approved to have another playground added to the sites. You will see within the item a list of the schools for this year's

projects. You will see that in the background paragraph there, it lists the various schools that will be benefiting from this contract. The current contract does expire October 31, 2026, and the new contract starts November 1, 2026, through October 31, 2027. This is actually the first renewal for this contract. Last year was the first year we put out the solicitation, and All Recreation of

Virginia is being renewed for another one year, to do these projects for Loudoun County Public Schools and work with our staff on the implementation of these playgrounds. We're asking that you either move this to your next meeting as an action or consent item, and then on the school board consent agenda on September 22nd, 2026. Thank you, Ms. Fillow. Any questions? And, oh, sure, Ms. McCartney. Thank you, Madam Chair. So,

how many firms were awarded this contract? The original award was two firms. We renewed with one firm. This firm has been doing a great job for us. Working with one vendor helps with scheduling. This vendor also has the staff capacity to do this many projects for us. They have proven that they were building up their resources to provide these services to us because there are a lot of schools on this list, and we are

confident that they can complete the work on time. Their pricing has been very favorable throughout the work as far as giving us good pricing on all the projects they've done for Loudoun County Public Schools during the past year. Okay, so this is 4.4 million. Actually, I'm good with it. I think I'm fine. Thank you. Any other questions?

If you are okay with it for consent, I would like to move it to our September 8th meeting. Is that okay? You guys okay with that? No. Oh, sure. Go ahead, Ms. McCartney. Sorry. This is all part of the CIP or the CAP? Actually, this is part of CIP, and you would still need to bring it to your September 15th meeting to have it be consent or action, and then you could put it on school board consent on September 22nd.

Okay. Thank you. Thank you for that correction. I thought we were going to try and move it to the 8th. Okay. So if you are okay with the 15th, we'll move it to consent then. Okay, we'll go ahead and do that. Thank you. Now we move to item 5.05, Business and Financial Services Renewal of RFP R25310, Construction Support Services. Again, Ms. Fillow, if you don't mind, Director of Procurement and Risk Management. Thank you.

Yes, this contract is for multiple vendors that are able to provide us construction support services at times of peak work or when we need additional assistance with managing projects. The current value of this contract is $600,000. The contract did allow for multiple awards. The current contract expires October 31, 2026. You will see the vendors listed in the summary section, and we are asking that you consider bringing this forward on your September 15th as action or consent, and

then once again to the school board consent on September 22nd. Any questions? Yes, Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. How do we decide when we need additional support which one of these firms we use? Is it by what their expertise are? Is it by cost of the contract? What's the determining factor- Yes ... of which one we use? It can be their expertise. It can also be the cost. It can also be availability. Okay. Who's available. Mr. Pasquarelli, if there's anything you'd like to add?

No. Go ahead. Okay. I just know we have a bunch of different contracts. I want to see how it is. Okay. I don't think I have anything else on this one. I do have a question on this, and I did have a little bit of a discussion with you, Mr. Treanor. The proposals are from 2024. So I'm looking for if we were to use any of these companies, where the updates would be on costs.

I don't think I saw that listed. There has been no rate increases. So the cost is contingent upon the work they are doing with us, but they have not increased their hourly rate to provide these services. Okay. It would depend on the number of hours that we need them. So there has been no rate increase. Oh, okay. Good to hear. That's what I was curious about, and I think that's it for my questions. How does everybody feel about consent?

We'll go ahead and do that. We'll move it to consent, and then we'll move on to 5.06, Business and Financial Services Renewal of RFP R26014, Job Order Contracting for General Construction. Ms. Fillow, Director of Procurement and Risk Management again. Thank you. The estimated value of this work is $7 million. You will see there are multiple vendors awarded on this contract, which once again,

as Mr. Pepper brought up, we distribute the work based on what we talked about during the previous item. This job order contract is actually the current contract term, expires December 31, 2026, so we're bringing it before you now to ensure it's in place for January 1, 2027. We would ask that you bring it forward at September 15th as an action or consent item and on the school board consent agenda on September 22nd, 2026.

Thank you. Any discussion? No. I did have one question. General construction. Can you give me an idea or examples of what they'd be working on as far as general construction? I could, but Mr. Pasquarelli's right there- Oh. Oh ... so I'm going to have him come up- Mr. Pasquarelli ... and give you some examples. Hi, good afternoon. So we use this contract for summer work for the most part.

So there may be a storage room at a school that we're converting to an office space or something like that. It may be a painting project during the summer, small to medium-sized projects. And the JOC program is a pre-negotiated unit price contract, meaning we know what it's going to cost us per square foot for painting and for a lineal foot of pipe, that kind of thing. So we use it for those types of projects.

Great. Thank you so much, Mr. Esterly. Did anybody have any questions after that? No. I think we can go ahead and move this to consent. How does everybody feel? Yep, we're good. We'll move that to consent as well. Now we move on to 5.07, Business and Financial Services Revision of Policy 4330, Remedies and Bids and Awards. Again, Ms. Filow, if you don't mind. Thank you.

Absolutely. So we're going to take you off of contracts now and on to the policies that help us with our contracts. The first one I'm presenting to you is Policy 4330, which is Remedies in Bids and Awards. This particular policy is really to clean up and align with the Virginia Public Procurement Act, and also make just some cosmetic changes. The information within here is also included in each of our solicitations when they go out regarding remedies in bids and awards, like the determination of

non-responsibility. So these things are incorporated into our solicitations, and once again, this is just clean up to align with the Virginia Public Procurement Act, which governs what we do. Thank you, Ms. Filow. Any questions? Ms. Ricardi? Thank you, Madam Chair. So, this is part of this whole group of procurement policies that we're in the process of looking through?

Yes, this would be my final two. Final two. Okay. I have questions, I think probably more for the next one, but I think they're going to wind up working for both. This is one I would actually not like to go to consent because I want to make sure I take a really good look at it. Because now with these two, we'll have the whole package, and I really want to take some time to make sure that all of the policies thread properly, and that there's

no gaps between the seams in some of these policies. So, what are the major changes that we've made to this one? The red lines will just represent the changes that were made, and once again, as I shared, it's just really to get it in line with the Virginia Public Procurement Act. For example, you will see that the policy related or the section related to a protest if a vendor doesn't agree with our award. It's just been moved down in the document to the more appropriate section.

You'll also see that it spells out that they have basically 10 days from the notice of intent of award to protest and what that process looks like. The determination, the debarment process also says for unsatisfactory performance. That is standard Virginia Public Procurement Act language along with when is a vendor non-responsible. And once again, this is just to reiterate what we have in our solicitation documents and what's in the state code.

Thank you. Yes, Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. This is really just a clarification question. How do we determine someone is a non-responsible bidder? A non-responsible bidder is a bidder that you would determine upfront they're not capable of doing the work. You may have some way of saying they only have two staff, and we need them to work 100 locations. Non-responsible is not used very often.

The main thing is with non-responsible, you must let the vendor know that they are non-responsible and give them an opportunity to disclaim that and say, "Well, I am responsible and here is why." But that is why it's written in Virginia Public Procurement Act so detailed as it is here in this policy to properly reflect if we were to make that determination. I appreciate that clarification. That was the one thing I was digging through this last night trying to figure out

what it was talking about there, but I appreciate that. Thank you. Thank you both. I had a couple of things, just verbiage. Well, the first thing is verbiage issues. Where you have he, she, his, her, you could put T-H-E-I-R. You could put their. That would fit. If you could just go ahead and do that rather than- We have actually stricken his, her in the red line. Yeah.

It's just the claim of right to withdraw. There is no reference to a pronoun there. Well, when I was reading it, it looked like you could put there if you needed to, if you wanted to. I'll also just share there's a division-wide approach to the policies that we are following related to the reference to pronouns. I don't see a problem with T-H-E-I-R. I understand that you're trying to follow something. What is it called again?

It's something specific, right? I can't remember the reference- I can't remember the reference either ... but I know Mr. Allen has mentioned it during school board meetings. But, again, we are just following that direction. Well, I really don't see an issue with T-H-E-I-R for every spot. I don't see how that's a problem. I will share what Ms. Ricardi shared- Uh-huh ... a point to show non-consistency among our other policies where we've done it

this way. I will add that. So Ms. Ricardi, when you brought up looking at all the policies, this is going to be worded different than the other ones I have. And we'll look forward to seeing the policy again. But also, I did have a question on, and this kind of threw me off a little bit. A bidder may withdraw his or her bid from consideration if the price

bid was substantially lower than other bids due solely to mistake herein, provided the bid was submitted in good faith and mistake was a clerical mistake. So basically what that's telling me is if they didn't win the bid and they want to, that would be a protest at that point, right? Or they won the bid, but it was lower than everybody else put in, and they want to move the cost up. Does that make sense?

During the 10-day protest period, which is after the notice of intent to award, vendors do have an opportunity to withdraw their bid if they have determined they made a mistake. That is when the opportunity presents itself for them to withdraw the bid. If they withdraw that bid because they can't hold that price or honor that price, we want them to withdraw their bid and not have them come back later and say, "Well, we need to increase our cost because we made a mistake." Therefore,

that 10-day window gives them that opportunity to withdraw their bid due to an error in calculations or any other type of error that they have discovered. What we actually do is when we prepare to award, we send out something to the vendor that says, "Okay, this is what you bid. Can you agree to this?" And they have that opportunity during that 10-day protest period or 10-day period to withdraw their bid. Thank you. That gives me more of an explanation on that because when you first read

it, it comes across like, "Oh, wait a minute, all the other bids were more. I want to change it and charge more." So, I just wanted to make that clarification. So, per our discussion, we'll have this come back to the finance and operations as an action item. Thank you. Thank you. Now we move on to 5.08, Business and Financial Services Revision of Policy 4340, Procurement Procedures. Again, Ms. Filow. Thank you.

Thank you. First, I would like to bring to your attention in the attachments I also included the current Policy 4340 and the Regulation 4340. What I wanted you to be aware of is in the regulation you will see where we have added those items that were stricken from Policy 4340. The regulation actually identifies the things that can and cannot, must be included in a contract or cannot be included in a contract. These help us make sure that we are in compliance with state code, once again, as

well as any legal policies or internal policies. The procurement exceptions is being brought to align with the State of Virginia process. Basically, this is the State of Virginia's document regarding what is exempt from the competitive procurement process up to a value of $200,000, or in the case of Section A, it's specific items. And then when you get down to the administrative

exemptions, it's up to $200,000. For example, you'll see in that list memberships and dues. If being a member of the Virginia School Board Association was more than $200,000 or less than $200,000, we wouldn't say go out and get three quotes and find the best organization to meet our needs. We pay that as part of being a school board or as I do as part of a procurement organization. In addition, you'll see postage. Postage is what postage is.

We have to pay what it costs per stamp or to mail something. Travel. For travel, we use per diem rates. So we have an established process. We use the federal guidelines regarding per diem rates, and you'll see various other things there on this list that are included. And then there's other non-procurement transactions that may require a requisition or purchase order but don't fall under the procurement services or the requirements of this policy, and you can see those there as well.

And I will open the floor for any questions you might have. You will notice we have changed this title to be Procurement Procedure Exemptions. And as I had said, this is in alignment with the State of Virginia code and the practices that State of Virginia follows along with the Virginia Public Procurement Act. Thank you, Ms. Fullilove. Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. Appreciate the hard work that went into this because we're basically rewriting this entire policy.

If you look at current 4340 and revised 4340, they are 100% different. My question is some of the stuff in old 4340 that pertains, for example, to people who are awarded a contract and might have an employee who is a criminal offender in some way, is that found elsewhere now in our policy? Because some of this is still important.

That is why I shared the regulation with you, because the regulation identifies everything that we should have included in a contract- Mm-hmm ... and those things we cannot agree to in the contract. So therefore, that section was moved to the associated regulation to better align with the other contract terms and conditions we must follow as a procurement organization in a K through 12. Appreciate that. Thank you. Any other questions? Yes, Ms. McRee.

Thank you for this. I appreciate it. And as I mentioned before, I do have a small number of proposed changes. I'll email those to you all so we can fold those into the next version of this or use it as amendments if we want to. So it sounds to me, and just make sure I understand, so we basically took out items from 4340 that are part of the legally required procurement process and moved

them into a regulation. It's a new regulation, or has it been there and it was revised? This is a regulation that has been there, and we revised it by adding these things in to go with the other things that were in that regulation. Okay. Thank you. And then on the list of administrative exemptions, can you give me some examples? What are educational films? What's included in educational films?

I would have to say educational films is probably a more outdated term, but educational would be, for example, if we adopted a certain curriculum or a certain leadership or something like that, it would be what goes with that. And basically what you're getting into is because you've aligned with that, you've put yourself in a sole source situation, right?

Because every vendor's going to say, "I can only provide you this." And that's what this has done here with this list. So are these educational training videos for our adults staff, or is this educational videos also for K through 12 educational purposes? I believe educational for us would be the student, staff, classrooms, because

down below on the red lines or item 13 on that list, you'll see tuition and training. So when you're talking about training for adults, tuition for adults, that's where I would say your training would fall. Okay. And is this list the same list, or are there any items on this list that are new or that were added? Or- This is the same list as the state.

Yes, it's pulled straight from state code. Okay. And then as far as legal services go, is that always been-- I believe it has been. It's always been on this list too. Yes, you're absolutely correct. The Virginia Public Procurement Act has actually excludes legal services from the procurement competitive requirements. And I see, yeah, and I see the number three on the front of this on page one. It says the approved textbooks.

That is correct. If they are on the VDOE list and we make a decision that's what we're going to utilize, we can purchase them through VDOE because the VDOE adopted and approved. Got it. Okay. Well, I'll go through and take a look. Yeah, this is one I definitely want to come back for action next time, so we can really get through this, but thank you for that. Go ahead, Ms. Willoughby. Just to sum up regarding both policies.

Both policies will now go through the public comment period where they'll be out there for public members to share any questions or concerns. As part of the process, this would automatically come back as action, and that, as Mr. Carty referred to earlier, in advance of our next meeting on the 15th, if you could share what amendments you may be entertaining, that will help us facilitate an efficient meeting on the 15th.

I think at this point, yeah, we'll have it come back as action to finance and operations. So thank you. Is there any new business? I wanted to just take some time just to, and I did speak to you a little bit about this, Ms. Willoughby. Just take some time to discuss the PTAs and the PTSOs. First off, I would like to thank them

for all their support, and we're talking booster clubs, PTSOs, PTAs, and school support organizations across Loudoun County for their extraordinary dedication and hard work. These volunteers provide countless opportunities, programs, and resources for our students that would otherwise not be available through LCPS funding alone. I think there's an issue that it appears like things are changing.

We'll need explanations as to why it's changing, but I understand and appreciate the division's desire to strengthen accountability and ensure consistency in fundraising practices. I believe the discussions that took place on August 13th warrant further clarification and additional stakeholder engagement. My concern is that if we proceed with the proposed memorandum agreement, the MOA, in its current form, we risk discouraging the very volunteers who contribute so

much to our schools. This is a 501 (c) (3) made up of volunteers, parents that want to see their students enjoy activities at their respective schools. Ms. Willoughby, I understand you are now in possession of the proposed agreement developed by Riverside High School? I'm in possession of feedback. Feedback. Okay. It's more of a negotiation, proposals and

negotiation. That's something that they'll want to use division-wide. So we'll have to continue those discussions. I am aware that you're having a meeting with Ms. Chernoff this Wednesday. I have not been privy to the details on that or included in that upcoming discussion. I would encourage LCPS administration to review that document that I just mentioned carefully and engage in discussions with our school support

organizations to determine whether it could serve as a model for division-wide agreement. That's why I mentioned it, because we're looking for it to serve division-wide. One other area it appears to be we need clarification for is parents or actually LCPS employees, will they continue to be permitted to hold leadership or volunteer roles with the PTSOs,

PTAs, and booster clubs while maintaining their employment with LCPS? So these are all things that I don't know what's going to be discussed on Wednesday, but we need to continue this discussion. It'll be on the agenda for our September 8th meeting, and in the interest of time, that was all I really wanted to bring up today about that subject. Unless you wanted to add something, Ms. Willoughby or Ms. Fullilove? Yes, I appreciate the opportunity to provide some additional context and clarity.

We also share the similar sentiment that we value our partnerships with our school support organizations. As you are aware, as I had shared over the past couple of weeks when you've shared the feedback that you were receiving, I am still available to meet at any time to have a further discussion. Similar to Ms. Chernoff, she reached out, and so I have set up a meeting with her. I welcome the opportunity to meet with you individually as well to address your

specific concerns. Related to the SSOs, we developed this Policy 8020 back in 2022. A lot of the concerns that are being shared now were also shared back then. Anytime we're implementing something new, there can be a fear of the unknown or a fear of change. However, back in October of 2024, at the Finance and Operations Committee meeting,

during that time when we were revising this policy, we publicly shared and had a lot of discussion how our next step was to develop this MOA. And actually, there was discussion about even creating a regulation. We have not created a regulation, but we did proceed over the last two years essentially, to develop the draft MOA. As part of that process, we were actively seeking feedback, and we are happy to see

that we are generating the feedback that we desire. We've had one initial stakeholder meeting with booster clubs that has generated some of the feedback that the board is also receiving, where really the process would be of sharing that feedback with staff, so that we can take that feedback and look for those opportunities to provide additional clarity to the agreement that we are wanting to put in place. We are working to schedule meetings with PTOs and then
